final_synthesis_description: All three stakeholders accept the core conditional middle path—pause, verify, seek legal/editorial review, and allow affected parties to respond before any publication—but converge on a stricter shared modification: if the document's provenance or lawful usability cannot be reasonably established, the default position is non-publication, and content accuracy alone is insufficient to justify publishing.
remaining_disagreements: Exact threshold for 'reasonably established' provenance remains undefined, leaving room for differing interpretations in edge cases
Degree of privacy minimization required (how much of the document's content may be used even when provenance is confirmed) is not fully specified
Whether a strong public interest justification can ever override uncertain provenance is not resolved among stakeholders
